new_statements.translation: But two oppositions by degree of aperture, e – ɛ and o – ɔ, can be reconstructed, because one can presume syllable tones in Pumpokol as in the other Yeniseian languages. In any case there are some indications of the second, laryngealised tone, to which the neutral first tone must have stood in opposition, and the existence of an opposition between these two tones was a good reason for the emergence of open and closed mid vowels. The following features point to the second tone in Pumpokol: 1. the diphthongisation in koat 'way' together with G. F. Müller's remark 'monosyl.', which clearly points to ²ko't, cf. Ket ²qot, Yugh ²xot 'way'. 2. the possible notation of the laryngeal stop with the grapheme g ...

new_statements.rule_in_words: No word-stress rule is stated. Werner treats Pumpokol, like every Yeniseian language, as a syllable-tone language and finds evidence in the 18th-century wordlists for a laryngealised 'second tone' contrasting with a neutral 'first tone'; word accent in his normalised Pumpokol forms is marked with an acute on varying syllables (xúta '1', dóŋa '3', xaiáŋ '10', hukút 'house', píkola 'daughter' per Wikipedia's transcription of Werner 2005), but no placement rule for it was found.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the whole statement is hedged ('vermuten kann', 'einige Hinweise') because the language is known only from 18th-century wordlists.
new_statements.domain_note: Extinct language reconstructed from c. 65 genuine 18th-century lexical items (Müller, Fischer, Strahlenberg, Pallas, Tatishchev questionnaires); the statement concerns isolated citation-form words. The quote is assembled from overlapping Google Books search snippets, not from an opened page; '0-0' in the snippet is the feed's rendering of the vowel pair (o – ɔ in the translation) and the superscript tone numerals appear as 2ko't, 2qot, 2xot. The sentence about 'kurzsilbigen Akzentuationstypen' found in the same book belongs to the Kott chapter, not to Pumpokol.
new_statements.identity_note: Pumpokol = Glottolog pump1237 / ISO xpm, a Yeniseian language of the upper Ket' river extinct by c. 1740, attested only in 18th-century wordlists (Messerschmidt, Strahlenberg, G. F. Müller, Fischer, Pallas, Tatishchev questionnaires; c. 65 genuine items). 'Pumpokol' was a volost' name, and part of the material so labelled is actually Yugh (yugh1239) as shown by Verner 1979 and Werner 2005 (Georg 2007: 18); Werner's chapter and the quoted passage concern the residue he identifies as genuinely Pumpokol. No dialects are distinguished.
